puzzles.title: Select Everything
puzzles.explanation: This query retrieves all columns and all rows from the 'users' table. The * wildcard means 'every column'.
puzzles.hint: Start with SELECT, then what columns, then where from.

puzzles.title: Pick One Column
puzzles.explanation: Instead of *, you can name a specific column. This returns only the 'username' column from 'users'.
puzzles.hint: Replace * with the column name you want.

puzzles.title: Two Columns
puzzles.explanation: You can select multiple columns by separating them with commas. This gets 'name' and 'email' from 'customers'.
puzzles.hint: Multiple columns are separated by commas before FROM.

puzzles.title: Filter Rows
puzzles.explanation: WHERE filters the rows returned. This returns only products where price is greater than 100.
puzzles.hint: WHERE comes after FROM and sets a condition.

puzzles.title: Exact Match
puzzles.explanation: Use = to match exact values. String values must be wrapped in single quotes like 'admin'.
puzzles.hint: Text values in SQL need single quotes around them.

puzzles.title: Count Rows
puzzles.explanation: COUNT(*) is an aggregate function that returns the total number of rows in the table.
puzzles.hint: COUNT is a function — it wraps * inside parentheses.

puzzles.title: Alias a Column
puzzles.explanation: AS renames a column in the result set. Here 'price' will appear as 'cost' in the output.
puzzles.hint: AS comes right after the column name you want to rename.

puzzles.title: Not Equal
puzzles.explanation: != means 'not equal to'. This returns all users who are NOT inactive.
puzzles.hint: != is the 'not equal' operator in SQL.

puzzles.title: Sort Results
puzzles.explanation: ORDER BY sorts the results. ASC means ascending (lowest to highest). Use DESC for the reverse.
puzzles.hint: ORDER BY comes after WHERE (or FROM if no WHERE).

puzzles.title: Limit Results
puzzles.explanation: LIMIT restricts how many rows are returned. Here only the first 10 rows are returned.
puzzles.hint: LIMIT always goes at the very end of the query.

puzzles.title: Top 5 Most Expensive
puzzles.explanation: Combining ORDER BY DESC and LIMIT gives you the top N rows. This gets the 5 most expensive products.
puzzles.hint: Sort descending first, then cut to 5 rows with LIMIT.

puzzles.title: Group By Category
puzzles.explanation: GROUP BY groups rows with the same value. This counts how many products exist in each category.
puzzles.hint: Any non-aggregate column in SELECT must appear in GROUP BY.

puzzles.title: Filter After Grouping
puzzles.explanation: HAVING filters groups after GROUP BY. Unlike WHERE, it can use aggregate functions like COUNT.
puzzles.hint: HAVING is like WHERE but for grouped results — it comes after GROUP BY.

puzzles.title: AND Condition
puzzles.explanation: AND combines conditions — both must be true. This finds shipped orders worth more than 200.
puzzles.hint: AND requires ALL conditions to be true.

puzzles.title: OR Condition
puzzles.explanation: OR returns rows where at least one condition is true. This gets admins and moderators.
puzzles.hint: OR means either condition can be true.

puzzles.title: Sum of Sales
puzzles.explanation: SUM adds up all values in a column. This calculates total revenue from completed orders only.
puzzles.hint: SUM is an aggregate function like COUNT.

puzzles.title: Average Score
puzzles.explanation: AVG calculates the mean. Here we also use AS to give the result a readable name.
puzzles.hint: AVG works like SUM but divides by the count automatically.

puzzles.title: Pattern Match
puzzles.explanation: LIKE with % wildcard matches patterns. % means 'any characters'. This finds all Gmail users.
puzzles.hint: LIKE is used for pattern matching, % is the wildcard.

puzzles.title: Inner Join
puzzles.explanation: INNER JOIN combines rows from two tables where the ON condition matches. Only users who have orders appear.
puzzles.hint: JOIN links tables, ON specifies the matching columns.

puzzles.title: Left Join
puzzles.explanation: LEFT JOIN returns all rows from the left table (users), even if there's no matching order. Missing orders show as NULL.
puzzles.hint: LEFT JOIN keeps all rows from the first (left) table.

puzzles.title: Join with Filter
puzzles.explanation: You can alias table names (users as u) to write shorter queries. WHERE still filters after the JOIN.
puzzles.hint: Table aliases go right after the table name. WHERE filters the joined result.

puzzles.title: Subquery in WHERE
puzzles.explanation: A subquery runs inside another query. Here we first calculate the average price, then find products above it.
puzzles.hint: The subquery in parentheses runs first and returns a single value.

puzzles.title: Group with Join
puzzles.explanation: This counts how many orders each user has made, including users with zero orders (LEFT JOIN returns NULL, COUNT ignores NULLs).
puzzles.hint: LEFT JOIN + GROUP BY + COUNT gives you per-user totals including zeros.

puzzles.title: Having with Join
puzzles.explanation: This finds users whose total spending exceeds 1000. HAVING filters after grouping, allowing aggregate conditions.
puzzles.hint: HAVING filters GROUPS. Use it when WHERE won't work with aggregate functions.

puzzles.title: Nested Subquery
puzzles.explanation: IN with a subquery checks if a value exists in a list. This finds users who placed at least one large order.
puzzles.hint: The subquery inside IN returns a list of IDs to match against.

puzzles.title: Full Aggregation Pipeline
puzzles.explanation: This is a full pipeline: group products by category, count them, average their prices, filter categories with 3+ products, sort by average price descending.
puzzles.hint: Remember the order: SELECT → FROM → GROUP BY → HAVING → ORDER BY.
